Introduction

Anti-Ahmadis often point to the British preacher John Hugh Smyth-Pigott. They claim:

“Mirza Ghulam Ahmad warned Smyth-Pigott that he would die in Ahmad’s lifetime if he claimed to be God. But Mirza Ghulam Ahmad died in 1908, while Smyth-Pigott lived until 1927. Therefore, the prophecy failed.”

This claim is completely false. Opponents deliberately hide the historical context, the terms of the challenge, and what Smyth-Pigott actually did.

When you examine the primary historical records from 1902 to 1909, the facts are clear:

• Bilateral challenge and conditional warning (Wa’eed): It was not an unconditional death prediction. It depended on Pigott accepting the challenge and persisting in his public claim of godhood.

• Pigott panicked and went into hiding: After the November 1902 warning, Pigott completely stopped preaching his divinity to the world. He fled London, hid behind 12-foot brick walls guarded by bloodhounds at Spaxton, and refused to answer letters or meet emissaries.

• The rule of warning prophecies in the Quran: When a transgressor is terrified, retreats, and halts his public defiance, God stays the immediate punishment. This is the exact principle of Prophet Jonah (Yunus (AS)) and the people of Nineveh in the Quran.

• Pigott was publicly ruined and kicked out of the Church: In March 1909, the Church of England put Pigott on trial and formally stripped him of his priesthood in Wells Cathedral in total public disgrace. His cult vanished, while the Ahmadiyya Movement spread across the globe.

Let us examine the full chronological story step by step.

September 7, 1902 – Smyth-Pigott Claims Divinity in London

Rev. John Hugh Smyth-Pigott was an ordained Church of England curate. In 1902, he took over a wealthy Victorian sect called the Agapemonites (“Abode of Love”) in Spaxton, Somerset. The sect controlled a massive fortune of over £100,000 and a luxurious 200-acre estate.

The sect built an ornate church in Clapton, London, called the Ark of the Covenant.

On Sunday, September 7, 1902, Pigott stood before a crowd of 6,000 people and declared:

“I am that Lord Jesus Christ who has come again in the body… Do not look for a Jesus who is in the heavens, for He is present among you.”

[The Hackney and Kingsland Gazette, September 10, 1902]

His followers prostrated before him. But the general public was outraged.

On September 14, 1902, thousands of angry protestors surrounded the church. Pigott was heckled, assaulted, and pelted with stones. The London police had to rush in and escort him away to save his life.

October 1902 – Hazrat Mufti Muhammad Sadiq (RA) Inquires from Qadian

In Qadian, India, Hazrat Mufti Muhammad Sadiq (RA) regularly monitored British journals. He read reports of Pigott’s blasphemous claim in British newspapers (The Freethinker).

Mufti Sadiq (RA) immediately sent a letter to Smyth-Pigott in London, inquiring whether the newspaper reports were accurate.

On October 22, 1902, during his morning walk, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) was informed about Pigott. Huzoor (AS) said:

اگر پگٹ ہمارا مقابلہ کرے تو بہت ہی کارآمد ہو… اگر اس کو چیلنج دیا جاوے اور چھاپا جاوے تو امید ہے کہ اللہ تعالیٰ کوئی نشان دکھاوے۔

“If Pigott opposes us it will be very beneficial… If he competes it will be very beneficial, and people will also pay heed… Compared to the Americans, the British are more linked with us. If he is challenged and in print, then it is hoped that Allah Almighty will show some Sign.”

[Al-Badr, November 21, 1902, pp. 28–29]
[Malfuzat, Vol. 3, pp. 374–375]

Notice the words used by Hazrat Ahmad (AS): “If he opposes us”, “if he competes”, and “if he is challenged”. This proves from day one that it was framed as an active spiritual contest.

November 11, 1902 – Pigott’s Secretary Replies with “Noah’s Ark”

On November 11, 1902, a reply arrived in Qadian from Pigott’s secretary, Mr. Douglas Hamilton.

Hamilton confirmed Pigott’s claim to divinity and enclosed two pamphlets distributed at their Clapton church. One leaflet was titled Noah’s Ark. It claimed that their London church was the only ark of salvation, and anyone outside would be spiritually destroyed.

When this was read out, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) remarked:

معقول بات کا اثر ہوتا ہے اور وہ قائم رہتی ہے اور لغو بات چند سطروں کے بعد اپنی جدّت کھو بیٹھتی ہے… اب ہماری نوح کی کشتی اس باطل کشتی پر غالب آئے گی۔

“Rational converse is respected and has lasting effect, but irrational thought loses its innovativeness in the space of a few lines… Now our true Ark of Noah will dominate the false Ark. Dowie is claiming to be a Prophet in America and Pigott is claiming to be God in London.”

[Al-Badr, November 21, 1902, pp. 28–29]
[Malfuzat, Vol. 3, p. 375]

(Note: Hazrat Ahmad’s famous book Kashti-e-Nuh (Noah’s Ark) was written and published during this exact period in October–November 1902).

November 24, 1902 – The Warning & Mubahala Challenge Sent to the UK

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) drafted an announcement titled “A Warning to a Pretender to Divinity”. It was translated into English by Maulana Muhammad Ali and dispatched to prominent British newspapers, including The Sunday Circle and The Daily News.

In this announcement, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) warned:

“God Almighty has informed me that claiming divinity is an insult to the Majesty of the Creator… If Mr. Pigott does not desist and repent from this claim, he will face divine destruction in my lifetime…”

[The Sunday Circle, February 14, 1903]
[Zikr-e-Habib, p. 83]

Hazrat Mufti Muhammad Sadiq (RA) wrote an accompanying letter directly to Smyth-Pigott, issuing a direct prayer duel (Mubahala):

“Repent from such a claim, which Jesus (AS) had not desired for himself, even rejecting the title of ‘good’ for himself, let alone ‘God’ [Matthew 19:17]… If you persist in your claim of divinity, then decree as one claiming to be divine that Mirza Ghulam Ahmad should die in your lifetime, inform him of this verdict, and ask him to also pray to God about this matter.”

[Al-Hakam, November 17, 1902]
[Al-Badr, November 21, 1902]

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) signed the announcement as “The Prophet, Mirza Ghulam Ahmad”, clearly pitting the true Prophet of God against the false pretender.

Late 1902 – Divine Revelations in Qadian

Around November 20, 1902, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) received revelations concerning Smyth-Pigott:

وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ • إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُحْسِنُونَ

“Allah is severe in retribution. They are not acting righteously.”

[Tadhkirah, p. 597]
[Al-Badr, November 21, 1902]

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) explained this revelation:

• Current evil: It indicated that Pigott’s current state was evil.

• Future persistence: Or, that he would not repent in the future.

• Humiliating end: His ultimate end would be doomed with humiliation.

Soon after, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) received another revelation promising divine protection for his own reputation:

وَلَا نُبْقِیْ لَکَ مِنَ الْمُخْزِیَاتِ ذِکْرًا

“We shall leave no trace of anything the allusion to which might reflect adversely upon your honour.”

[Tadhkirah, p. 786]

Late 1902–1906 – Pigott Panics, Flees London, and Barricades at Spaxton

How did Smyth-Pigott respond to the November 1902 warning and public backlash? He panicked, ran away, and went completely silent:

• Abandoned London: He shut down public preaching at the Ark of the Covenant in Clapton and fled to the countryside in Spaxton, Somerset.

• Hidden behind 12-foot walls: He locked himself inside the Spaxton estate behind 12-foot-high brick walls guarded by bloodhounds.

• Refused all emissaries: An emissary traveled 7,000 miles from India to meet Pigott in person to demand a response to the challenge. Pigott refused to open the doors.

• Refused registered mail: Official letters and summons sent to Pigott were rejected at the post office by his secretary.

How Opponents’ Own Newspaper Proofs Turn Against Them

Critics try to quote British newspapers from 1904, 1905, and 1906 to claim Pigott was still preaching divinity. But when you actually read the exact words of those very newspapers, they prove the exact opposite—they prove Pigott had completely stopped public preaching!

Look at what the primary records between 1904 and 1906 actually reported:

1. Taunton Courier and Western Advertiser (June 29, 1904)

“He rarely appears outside the walls of his carefully guarded temple of mystery.”

[Taunton Courier, June 29, 1904]

The journalists admitted Pigott was terrified, hiding behind high walls, and never coming out to preach to the public.

2. The Chard and Ilminster News (September 15, 1906)

“He feared leakages in a printing office by which his special messages might get to the outer world… The result of all this secrecy and precaution is that extracts from these notes have never been published.”

[The Chard and Ilminster News, September 15, 1906]

This newspaper explicitly confirms Pigott was so terrified of public backlash that he stopped printing anything and banned his words from ever reaching the outer world!

3. Academic Historian Dr. Joshua Schwieso (Deluded Inmates)

“Smyth-Pigott had learned his lesson at Clapton, that the opinion of the outside world still counted and he had no desire to face in Somersetshire the kind of demonstrations he had endured in London… When he drove through the village he adopted the worldly role of a benign squire rather than that of the Messiah.”

[Deluded Inmates, p. 171]

May 23, 1908 – Hazrat Ahmad’s (AS) Verdict 3 Days Before Demise

On May 23, 1908, just three days before his passing, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) delivered a public address in Lahore. He praised Hazrat Mufti Muhammad Sadiq (RA) and declared:

مفتی محمد صادق صاحب کو اشاعت سلسلہ کا بڑا درد ہے۔ کوئی جگہ انگلستان میں ایسی نہیں جہاں انہوں نے انگریزی دانوں یا اخباروں کے ایڈیٹروں سے خط و کتابت کر کے حضرت اقدس کے دعوے نہ پہنچائے ہوں۔ چنانچہ امریکہ کے ڈوئی کا عبرتناک انجام اور لندن کے پگٹ کی ذلت آمیز ناکامی انہی مکرم مفتی صاحب کی کوششوں کا نتیجہ ہے۔

“Mufti Muhammad Sadiq has a burning desire for the propagation of the Ahmadiyya Movement, and there is hardly any place in England where he has not corresponded with English researchers or editors of newspapers and communicated to them the claims of the Promised Messiah (AS). The sorrowful ending of Dowie of America and the pathetic failure of Pigott of London are the result of the efforts of the respected Mufti [Sadiq] Sahib. While he was the cause of destruction of Pigott and Dowie, he was also the cause of guidance for many fortunate souls.”

[Al-Hakam, June 6, 1908]
[Malfuzat, Vol. 10, pp. 563–564]

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) did not view the Pigott affair as unfulfilled. He saw Pigott’s terror, his retreat into hiding, and his pathetic failure (zillat-ameez nakaami) as the clear realization of the warning.

January–March 1909 – Pigott Put on Trial and Stripped of Priesthood

In 1908, Pigott fathered two illegitimate children (“Glory” and “Power”) with his young follower Ruth Preece while living in his commune.

The Bishop of Bath and Wells (George Wyndham Kennion) took legal action against him.

• The Trial (January 20, 1909): Presided over by Chancellor Chadwyck-Healey, K.C., in the Consistory Court of Wells Cathedral. Pigott was found guilty on all charges of gross immoral conduct and adultery.

• The Judgment (March 6, 1909): The Bishop of Bath and Wells formally stripped Pigott of his priesthood and expelled him from the Church of England in Wells Cathedral in front of the entire nation.

Pigott was disgraced as an immoral hypocrite and lived in total isolation until his death in 1927.

The Ultimate Contrast: Two Legacies

• The Agapemone (Smyth-Pigott): Pigott died in 1927 in obscurity. Ruth Preece tried to maintain the cult until her death in 1956. The estate was sold off to pay debts. Today, the sect is 100% extinct with zero followers worldwide. The Spaxton chapel is now a private storage shed.

• Ahmadiyyat (Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS)): In 1905, London’s Victoria Institute predicted Ahmad’s movement would decline after his death. Instead, the community flourished across the globe. In 1924, the community built London’s first purpose-built mosque (Fazl Mosque) under Khilafat.

On the front of London’s Fazl Mosque, the community inscribed in Persian: “There is Peace in this Abode of Love”—reclaiming true spiritual peace in the very country where Pigott’s false “Abode of Love” collapsed.

Dismantling Opponent Claims

Claim 1: “It was not a Mubahala, but an unconditional prophecy that Pigott MUST DIE in Ahmad’s lifetime.”

The Refutation:

This objection ignores the fundamental rules of divine warning prophecies (Wa’eed):

1. Hazrat Ahmad (AS) explicitly framed it as a challenge

On October 22, 1902, Huzoor (AS) said:

“If Pigott opposes us it will be very beneficial… If he competes it will be very beneficial, and people will also pay heed… Compared to the Americans, the British are more linked with us. If he is challenged and in print, then it is hoped that Allah Almighty will show some Sign.”

[Al-Badr, November 21, 1902, pp. 28–29]
[Malfuzat, Vol. 3, pp. 374–375]

2. Mufti Sadiq’s (RA) letter demanded a bilateral prayer duel

Pigott was asked directly: “If you are divine, decree that Mirza Ghulam Ahmad should die in your lifetime and pray against him.”

3. The Quranic rule of warning prophecies (The Jonah Principle)

In the Quran, Prophet Jonah (Yunus (AS)) warned the people of Nineveh that they would be destroyed within 40 days. The prophecy contained no stated conditions. Yet, when the people repented and humbled themselves in fear, God lifted the destruction:

فَلَوْلَا كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَا إِيمَانُهَا إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّا آمَنُوا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا

“Why was there no other people, save the people of Jonah, who believed so that their belief profited them? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of ignominy in the present life…”

[Surah Yunus, 10:98]

Did Prophet Jonah’s prophecy “fail”? No! Warning prophecies (Wa’eed) are meant to reform and warn. When the transgressor desists and hides in terror, capital punishment is stayed.

4. The contrast with John Alexander Dowie

• Dowie (USA): Accepted the duel, continued publishing attacks against Islam in Leaves of Healing, and prayed for the destruction of Muslims ➔ Struck by paralysis, ruined, and died in misery in March 1907 during Ahmad’s (AS) lifetime.

• Pigott (UK): Panicked, refused the challenge, never prayed against Ahmad (AS), fled into hiding, and stopped all public claims.

Claim 2: “Pigott did not repent, so he should have died.”

The Refutation:

Opponents misunderstand what “repentance” (Ruju’) means in prophecy:

1. Repentance does not mean converting to Islam

Millions of Christians and atheists do not accept Islam and do not drop dead. God does not force anyone to convert to Islam on pain of immediate death.

In prophetic duels, repentance means retreating from the specific transgressing act that provoked the warning—namely, publicly claiming to be God to the world.

Hazrat Ahmad (AS) explained this regarding Abdullah Atham:

“It should be remembered that his retraction was from calling the Holy Prophet ﷺ the Antichrist (Dajjal) and not from Christianity. The actual basis of this prophecy hinged upon this word—a word which he had taken back when the prophecy was made.”

[Al-Hakam, November 17, 1902, p. 5]
[Ruhani Khaza’in, Vol. 9, p. 248]

2. Pigott completely ceased claiming divinity in public

• Opponents’ own newspaper proofs turn against them: The newspapers from 1904 to 1906 (Taunton Courier, The Chard and Ilminster News) prove Pigott was hiding behind 12-foot walls and banned his words from ever reaching the outer world.

• Civil legal records: On official birth certificates in 1905 and 1908, Pigott legally signed his profession as “Priest in Holy Orders”—an ordinary Anglican priest, not God.

• Personal Bible inscription: In a Bible gifted to his son David, Pigott wrote: “To my first born son, David from your father who says with you ‘Our Father, Which art in Heaven.'” He openly confessed that God was in Heaven, distinct from himself.

• Academic consensus: Historians (e.g. Dr. Joshua Schwieso in Deluded Inmates) confirm Pigott completely retreated from his divinity claims after the 1902 London riots.

3. Exposing the Donald McCormick Hoax (“I am God; it does not matter what they do”)

• Opponents claim Pigott declared during his 1909 trial: “I am God; it does not matter what they do.”

• This quote is a complete fabrication. In the Somerset Archives (Ref: D/D/bd/37), the trial transcripts and newspaper records show Pigott never attended the trial and never made this statement.

• The quote first appeared 53 years later in a sensationalist 1962 book (Temple of Love) by Donald McCormick. McCormick is widely recognized by historians as a fraudulent writer who fabricated historical sources.

4. The Consistory Court could not charge him with blasphemy

Under English law, blasphemy required public utterance or publication. The Bishop of Bath and Wells could not prosecute Pigott for blasphemy because Pigott had completely stopped public preaching! They had to prosecute him under the Clergy Discipline Act 1892 for private moral misconduct instead.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Mirza Ghulam Ahmad’s prophecy about John Hugh Smyth-Pigott fail?

No. The warning issued to Smyth-Pigott in November 1902 was a conditional warning (Wa’eed) and a bilateral challenge against his public claim to divinity. Following the warning, Pigott panicked, fled London, locked himself behind closed walls at Spaxton, and ceased all public claims to godhood. Under Quranic law (Surah Yunus 10:98), when a transgressor desists and retreats in fear, the immediate capital punishment is averted.

Why didn’t Smyth-Pigott die before Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS)?

Because Smyth-Pigott retreated from his public claim and refused to accept the challenge or pray against Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS). In contrast, John Alexander Dowie in America accepted the duel, continued attacking Islam, and died a miserable death in 1907 during Hazrat Ahmad’s (AS) lifetime. Pigott was instead humiliated, prosecuted under the Clergy Discipline Act 1892, and formally stripped of his priesthood in Wells Cathedral in 1909.

Did Smyth-Pigott continue claiming to be God after 1902?

No. Historical records, civil birth certificates from 1905 and 1908, and academic studies by Dr. Joshua Schwieso prove that Pigott never made a public claim of divinity after 1902. On official documents, he designated himself merely as a “Priest in Holy Orders” and inscribed his son’s Bible with prayers to “Our Father in Heaven.”

Did Smyth-Pigott say “I am God; it does not matter what they do” in 1909?

No. That quote is a modern myth fabricated in 1962 by author Donald McCormick. Primary court records in the Somerset Archives (Ref: D/D/bd/37) prove that Pigott did not even attend his 1909 Consistory Court trial, and zero contemporary 1909 newspapers record any such statement.

30-Second Debate Conclusion

If anyone brings up the Smyth-Pigott prophecy in a debate, give them these 4 quick facts:

• Pigott ran away and shut his mouth: Unlike Dowie, who accepted the duel and died in 1907, Pigott ran away from London, hid behind 12-foot walls at Spaxton, and never preached divinity to the world again.

• Prophecies of punishment are conditional (Wa’eed): In Surah Yunus (10:98), when the people of Nineveh feared the warning of Prophet Jonah, God spared them from death. Pigott was terrified and halted his public claims.

• Publicly disgraced and kicked out of Church: In 1909, the Church of England put Pigott on trial and publicly stripped him of his priesthood in Wells Cathedral for gross immorality.

• Extinct cult vs. Global community: Pigott’s Agapemone sect is 100% extinct today. The Ahmadiyya Muslim Community built London’s first mosque in 1924 and continues to expand across the world under Khilafat.

Introduction

Is Dajjal Satan? Non-Ahmadis believe that Dajjal is not mentioned in the Quran.

However, we Ahmadis believe that the Quran is a complete book and mentions him clearly.

This is especially true because Ahadith describe Dajjal as the biggest fitnah ever created since Adam (AS), and every single prophet warned his people about him. How could Allah reveal a complete book of guidance and ignore the biggest trial Muslims would ever face?

The truth is simple: the Quran does mention Dajjal. The Quran reveals that Dajjal is actually a manifestation of Satan.

Is Dajjal Satan? Proof 1: Satan – The Deceiver

Lexically, the word Dajjal refers to someone who deceives, lies, and covers truth with falsehood.

The Holy Quran calls Satan the biggest deceiver: Al-Gharoor.

یٰۤاَیُّہَا النَّاسُ اِنَّ وَعۡدَ اللّٰہِ حَقٌّ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّکُمُ الۡحَیٰوۃُ الدُّنۡیَا ٝ وَلَا یَغُرَّنَّکُمۡ بِاللّٰہِ الۡغَرُوۡرُ

“O ye men, assuredly the promise of Allah is true, so let not the present life deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you with respect to Allah.”

[Holy Quran 35:5]

Allah repeats this exact same warning in Surah Luqman:

فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّکُمُ الۡحَیٰوۃُ الدُّنۡیَا ٝ وَلَا یَغُرَّنَّکُمۡ بِاللّٰہِ الۡغَرُوۡرُ

“So let not worldly life beguile you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.”

[Holy Quran 31:33]

Just as the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warned that Dajjal is the great deceiver, the Holy Quran calls Satan Al-Gharoor (the Deceiver).

Every Prophet Warned About Dajjal

The Quran tells us that every prophet warned his people about Satan. Ahadith confirm that these exact same prophets warned their people about Dajjal.

Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said about Dajjal:

إِنِّي لأُنْذِرُكُمُوهُ وَمَا مِنْ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ قَدْ أَنْذَرَهُ قَوْمَهُ، لَقَدْ أَنْذَرَ نُوحٌ قَوْمَهُ

“I warn you against him (i.e. the Dajjal) and there was no prophet but warned his nation against him. No doubt, Noah warned his nation against him.”

[Sahih al-Bukhari 3337]

Now see what the Holy Quran says about every prophet:

وَلَقَدۡ بَعَثۡنَا فِیۡ کُلِّ اُمَّۃٍ رَّسُوۡلًا اَنِ اعۡبُدُوا اللّٰہَ وَاجۡتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوۡتَ

“And We did raise among every people a Messenger, preaching: ‘Worship Allah and shun the Evil One [Taghut/Satan]…'”

[Holy Quran 16:36]

If Dajjal and Satan were two completely different entities, the Quran and Hadith would contradict each other. But they agree: every prophet warned against Satan, who reaches his peak deception in the latter days as Dajjal.

Satan Flips Good and Evil

Ahadith tell us that Dajjal will deceive people by showing them Hell and Paradise. What seems like Hell is actually Paradise, and what seems like Paradise is actually Hell:

الدَّجَّالُ أَعْوَرُ الْعَيْنِ الْيُسْرَى جُفَالُ الشَّعَرِ مَعَهُ جَنَّةٌ وَنَارٌ فَنَارُهُ جَنَّةٌ وَجَنَّتُهُ نَارٌ

“Dajjal is blind of left eye with thick hair and there would be a garden and fire with him and his fire would be a garden and his garden would be fire.”

[Sahih Muslim 2934a]

This act of flipping good and evil is the exact tactic of Satan:

تَاللّٰہِ لَقَدۡ اَرۡسَلۡنَاۤ اِلٰۤی اُمَمٍ مِّنۡ قَبۡلِکَ فَزَیَّنَ لَہُمُ الشَّیۡطٰنُ اَعۡمَالَہُمۡ

“By Allah, We did send Messengers to the peoples before thee; but Satan made their works appear beautiful to them…”

[Holy Quran 16:63]

What seems like paradise with Dajjal—worldly luxuries, godless freedom, and materialism—is actually spiritual fire. What seems like fire—submitting to God, praying, and self-restraint—is true paradise.

Dajjal and Satan Lead People Astray

Ahadith describe that Dajjal will lead people astray and make evil deeds appear good.

The Holy Quran mentions this as the direct promise of Satan:

وَلَاُضِلَّنَّہُمۡ وَلَاُمَنِّیَنَّہُمۡ

“‘And assuredly I will lead them astray and assuredly I will excite in them vain desires…'”

[Holy Quran 4:119]

Dajjal does not have magical powers. His whole deception is the fulfillment of Satan’s promise to lead humans away from Allah through vain desires.

Salaf: Dajjal is Satan

This is not a new claim invented by Ahmadis. Early scholars of the Salaf said the exact same thing.

Hafiz Nu’aim ibn Hammad (the teacher of Imam Bukhari) recorded the view of the companion Miqdam ibn Ma’dikarib (RA) and his students:

لَيْسَ هُوَ إِنْسَانٌ، إِنَّمَا هُوَ شَيْطَانٌ

“[Dajjal] is not human, rather he is a Satan.”

[Kitab al-Fitan by Nu’aim ibn Hammad, Hadith #1498 (Arabic Scan)] | [Urdu Scan]

Kitab al-Fitan Hadith 1498: The Salaf confirm Dajjal is not human, but Satan.

Even the Sahaba and early Salaf knew that Dajjal could never be a literal human monster. They clearly said he is Satan!

Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) on Dajjal

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) explained the true reality of Dajjal:

“The word Dajjal has two connotations: First, it signifies a group which supports falsehood and works with cunning and deceit. Secondly, it is the name of the Satan who is the father of all falsehood and corruption.“

[Haqiqat-ul-Wahi, Ruhani Khazain, vol. 22, p. 326]

He further explained:

“Thus the Dajjal who is mentioned in the Ahadith is none other than the Satan who will be slain in the latter days. As Christianity is the perfect manifestation of Satan, Surah Al-Fatihah makes no mention of Dajjal, but prescribes supplication against the mischief of the Christians [Al-Dallin]…”

[Haqiqat-ul-Wahi, Ruhani Khazain, vol. 22, p. 326]

You can read his full explanation and complete references in our article: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) on Dajjal.

Conclusion

Unlike non-Ahmadis, we believe the Holy Quran is a complete book. It tells us about the biggest fitnah that humans will ever face.

Dajjal is Satan. And in the latter days, he manifested in the form of Christian missionaries spreading the lie that God has a son, backed by global materialism.

Introduction

Abu Muhammad Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Sa’id ibn Hazm al-Andalusi al-Zahiri (d. 456 AH / 1064 CE) is celebrated throughout Islamic history as one of the most brilliant and uncompromising jurists of classical Islam. Renowned for his strict adherence to the literal text of the Holy Quran and authentic Sunnah, Ibn Hazm refused to accept theological claims that lacked direct textual proof.

When addressing the conclusion of the earthly life of Prophet Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him, Ibn Hazm arrived at the undeniable conclusion: Jesus of Nazareth died a natural death.

The Foundational Rule: Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul. It never means the taking of the body & soul.

Ibn Hazm proved this foundational linguistic and theological reality through strict deductive analysis of the Holy Quran itself.

Ibn Hazm’s Definitive Ruling in Al-Muhalla

In his masterwork of Islamic jurisprudence and theology, Al-Muhalla bi’l-Athar, Ibn Hazm writes:

وعيسى عليه السلام لم يُقتل ولم يُصلب، ولكن توفاه الله عز وجل ثم رفعه إليه، قال تعالى: {وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ}، وقال عز وجل: {إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ}، وقال تعالى عنه أنه قال: {فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنْتَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ}، وقال تعالى: {اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا}، فالوفاة ضربان: نوم، وموت فقط، فلم يرد عيسى بقوله: {فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي} وفاة النوم، فصح أنه إنما عنى وفاة الموت، ومن قال إنه عليه السلام قُتل أو صُلب فهو كافر مرتد حلال الدم والمال لمكذبته القرآن وخلافه الإجماع

“Jesus, peace be upon him, was neither killed nor crucified. Rather, Allah took him and raised him to Himself. Allah said: ‘They neither killed nor crucified him’ (Quran 4:157) and He, the Exalted, said: ‘I will take you to Me and lift you up to Me’ (Quran 3:55).

And He, the Exalted, said of him that he (Jesus) said: ‘When You took me to You, You became Watcher over them, and You are a Witness over everything’ (Quran 5:117), and Allah the Most High said: ‘Allah takes the souls at the time of their death and those who do not die in their sleep’ (Quran 39:42).

So there are two types of wafat: sleep and death alone.

And with his statement ‘when You took me’ (Quran 5:117) Jesus did not mean the wafat of sleep.

It is therefore correct that the wafat of death applies to him.

And whoever says that he (Jesus, peace be upon him) was killed or crucified is an unbelieving apostate, his blood is permitted (to be shed) and likewise his wealth is permitted (to be taken) because he has refuted the Quran and opposed the consensus.”

— [al-Muḥallā bi’l-Āthār, vol. 1, p. 43, mas’alah 32]

The Deductive Logic of Ibn Hazm

Ibn Hazm’s argument is rooted in rigorous logic and linguistic precision:

• Only Two Types of Wafat Exist: In Surah az-Zumar (39:42), Allah explicitly defines wafat when applied to living human beings as being of two categories only: the temporary taking of the soul during sleep, or the permanent taking of the soul at death. The Quran knows no third category of “taking physical body and soul into the sky.”

• Jesus Did Not Mean Sleep: In Surah al-Ma’idah (5:117), Jesus speaks on the Day of Judgment to Allah, recounting his departure from his community after which his followers corrupted his teachings. It is impossible that Jesus meant sleep, because sleep is a temporary state after which a prophet wakes up and remains among his people.

• The Unavoidable Conclusion: Since Jesus did not mean sleep, the only remaining category is the wafat of death. Therefore, Jesus (AS) died a natural death before his followers went astray.

Ibn Hazm on the Absence of Consensus (Ijma)

Many modern critics claim that there is a unanimous consensus (Ijma) among Muslims that Isa (AS) is alive in the sky. However, Ibn Hazm himself refuted this assumption centuries ago.

In his classical treatise on consensus, Maratib al-Ijma, Ibn Hazm explicitly documented:

واختلفوا في عيسى عليه السلام هل يأتي قبل يوم القيامة أم لا

“And they [the Ummah] differed regarding Jesus (peace be upon him), whether he will come before the Day of Judgment or not.”

— [Marātib al-Ijmā‘, p. 173]

This proves beyond all doubt that classical scholars recognized the widespread diversity of opinion on this subject, and that the belief in the natural death of Isa (AS) has deep roots among the foremost authorities of the Sunni tradition.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Ibn Hazm believe Isa (AS) was taken bodily to heaven?

No. In al-Muhalla, Ibn Hazm categorizes wafat into only two types based on Quran 39:42: sleep and death. Because Jesus in Quran 5:117 could not have meant sleep, Ibn Hazm concluded that the wafat of death definitively applied to him.

What is the Arabic rule for Tawaffa?

Tawaffa is an Arabic verb that means to take something. When Allah takes (does Tawaffi of) a human, it ONLY means taking of the soul. It never means the taking of the body & soul.

Did Ibn Hazm affirm an Ijma on Jesus being physically alive?

No. In his famous book Maratib al-Ijma (p. 173), Ibn Hazm explicitly recorded that the scholars differed on whether Jesus would return before the Day of Judgment, confirming that no consensus exists on his physical presence in the heavens.

Introduction

According to the Quran, Isa (as) and his Mother both used to eat food.

مَّا ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُۥ صِدِّيقَةٌۭ ۖ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَ ۗ ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱنظُرْ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ ٧٥
The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; other messengers had come and gone before him; his mother was a virtuous woman; both used to eat food [like other mortals]. See how clear We make these signs for them; see how deluded they are.

[Quran 5:75]

According to the Quran, all Messengers were given bodies that required food:

وَمَا جَعَلْنَـٰهُمْ جَسَدًۭا لَّا يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ خَـٰلِدِينَ ٨
We did not give them bodies that ate no food, nor were they immortal.

[Quran 21:8]

Argument

The Argument: Isa (as) Cannot Be Bodily Alive in Heaven

• Premise 1 (Quran 5:75): The Quran states that both Isa (as) and his mother Mary “used to eat food” (كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ الطَّعَامَ), grouping them together in the same grammatical construction and the same category of being.

• Premise 2 (Quran 21:8): The Quran establishes a general rule for all messengers — they were given real bodies that require food, and none of them were made immortal (“nor were they immortal”).

• Premise 3 (Shared grammar): Because 5:75 uses a dual verb form (كَانَا — “the two of them used to”) applied jointly to Isa and Mary, Arabic grammar requires that whatever is true of one regarding this action must be true of the other. They cannot be separated in status.

• The dilemma this creates for non-Ahmadi belief:

• If Isa (as) is bodily alive in heaven, then as a human body he must still require and eat food there.

• But the verse pairs him with Mary using the same verb — so if he is still eating/alive, she must be too.

• No non-Ahmadi Muslim believes Mary (as) is bodily alive in heaven today.

• Therefore, by the logic of the shared verb, Isa (as) cannot be bodily alive in heaven either.

• Only two consistent readings remain:

• Both Isa and Mary are alive in heaven and both still eat food — a position no one holds, and one that contradicts 21:8’s statement that messengers are not immortal.

• Both Isa and Mary lived, ate food as mortals, and both died a natural death — leaving neither alive in heaven today.

• Reinforcement from 21:8: The phrase “nor were they immortal” directly undercuts the idea of Isa (as) having a 2000-year uninterrupted physical life in heaven, especially when contrasted with the accepted death of Prophet Muhammad (saw).

Conclusion

Since no non-Ahmadi scholar claims Mary (as) is alive in the heavens, and the Quran grammatically ties her fate to Isa’s in this verse, consistency demands concluding that both died natural deaths — refuting the belief that Isa (as) remains bodily alive in heaven awaiting a second coming.

Introduction

Khalā (خلا) means to pass away. In the context of a human passing away, it only means the following:

• Passing away from this worldly life (i.e. death or martyrdom).

• Passing away from a specific location, IF that location is mentioned.

It is never used to describe flying physically towards heaven.

In Surah Al Imran, Allah Almighty establishes a universal divine law regarding all prophets:

وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ

“And Muhammad is only a Messenger. Verily, all Messengers have passed away before him. If then he die or be slain, will you turn back on your heels?”

[Quran 3:144]

When the Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away, the Muslim community was plunged into deep shock and grief. Hazrat Umar (RA) could not accept his death. He drew his sword and declared that the Prophet ﷺ had only gone to his Lord like Moses (AS) and would return.

Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) stepped forward and addressed the entire assembly. He recited Quran 3:144. Hearing this verse, every single Companion—including Hazrat Umar (RA)—accepted that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had truly died. Why? Because every previous messenger before him had already died.

This moment established the very first unanimous consensus (Ijmāʿ) of Islam: no prophet remains physically alive.

[!NOTE]
The Burden of Proof:
Anyone claiming that a past prophet was exempted from death and taken physically alive into heaven carries the entire burden of proof. There is zero Quranic verse and zero authentic Hadith stating that any prophet escaped death. In this guide, we examine the linguistic force of Al-Rusul (الرُّسُلُ), how Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) applied it, and why this dismantles the myth of a physically living Jesus in heaven.

The Meaning of Al-Rusul (الرُّسُلُ)

In Arabic, Al-Rusul (الرُّسُلُ) translates to “the Messengers.” The prefix Al- (الـ) on a plural noun can serve two functions:

• Lām al-Istighrāq (Total Inclusiveness): Referring to every single individual within that category without exception (“all the messengers”).

• Lām al-Jins (Generic Category): Referring to the class or category as a general concept.

In Quran 3:144, the prefix is definitively Lām al-Istighrāq. It encompasses all messengers without a single exception.

Why Al-Rusul Means Every Single Messenger

Al-Rusul cannot refer to a mere generic class or “some messengers” for three decisive reasons:

• The Internal Quranic Definition: The verse explicitly defines khalat through two exhaustive outcomes: “If then he die or be slain”. Allah outlines natural death (māta) or martyrdom (qutila). No third state—such as bodily ascension to the clouds—is mentioned.

• Comparison with Quran 5:75: Allah uses this exact same phrasing to establish the mortality and death of Isa (AS):

مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ الطَّعَامَ

“The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a Messenger; surely, all Messengers have passed away before him. And his mother was a truthful woman. They both used to eat food. See how We explain the Signs for their good, and see how they are turned away.”

[Quran 5:75]

In Quran 5:75, the phrase refers to all past messengers to prove that Isa (AS) was a mortal prophet like them. Both he and his mother ate food. Because they no longer eat food, they have passed away.

• The Logical Requirement of the Argument: If Al-Rusul only meant “some messengers,” Hazrat Abu Bakr’s (RA) argument would have fallen flat. Hazrat Umar (RA) could easily have answered: “Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is simply one of the exceptions!” The argument only works because Al-Rusul includes every single prophet without exception.

The Event of the Ijma of the Sahaba

The authentic Hadith collections record the tragic day the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away. They document how Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) established the death of all previous prophets through Quran 3:144.

1. The Passing of the Prophet ﷺ and Hazrat Umar’s (RA) Initial Denial

Hazrat Aisha (RA) described the final moments of the Holy Prophet Muhammad ﷺ:

…فَبَيْنَمَا رَأْسُهُ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ عَلَى مَنْكِبَيَّ إِذْ مَالَ رَأْسُهُ نَحْوَ رَأْسِي، فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ مِنْ رَأْسِي حَاجَةً، فَخَرَجَتْ مِنْ فِيهِ نُطْفَةٌ بَارِدَةٌ، فَوَقَعَتْ عَلَى ثُغْرَةِ نَحْرِي، فَاقْشَعَرَّ لَهَا جِلْدِي، فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ، فَسَجَّيْتُهُ ثَوْبًا، فَجَاءَ عُمَرُ وَالْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ شُعْبَةَ، فَاسْتَأْذَنَا، فَأَذِنْتُ لَهُمَا، وَجَذَبْتُ إِلَيَّ الْحِجَابَ، فَنَظَرَ عُمَرُ إِلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ: وَاغَشْيَاهْ، مَا أَشَدَّ غَشْيَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، ثُمَّ قَامَا، فَلَمَّا دَنَوَا مِنَ الْبَابِ، قَالَ الْمُغِيرَةُ: يَا عُمَرُ، مَاتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: كَذَبْتَ، بَلْ أَنْتَ رَجُلٌ تَحُوسُكَ فِتْنَةٌ، إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ حَتَّى يُفْنِيَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ…

“…One day, the Prophet was resting his head on my shoulder. Suddenly his head tilted towards mine. A cold drop came from his mouth and fell upon my chest, making my skin shiver. Thinking he had fainted, I covered him with a sheet.

Then Umar and Mughirah bin Shu’bah came and asked permission to enter. I permitted them and drew my curtain. Looking at the Prophet, Umar said: ‘Alas, the fainting! How severe is the fainting of the Messenger of Allah!’

They stood up to leave. As they drew near the door, Mughirah bin Shu’bah said: ‘O Umar, the Messenger of Allah has passed away.’ Umar replied: ‘You lie! Rather, you are stirred by trial. The Messenger of Allah will not die until Allah Almighty destroys the hypocrites.’“

[Musnad Ahmad 25841] | Grade: Hasan

2. Hazrat Umar’s (RA) Oath and His Belief in the Prophet’s ﷺ Return

Hazrat Aisha (RA) reported what happened in the Prophet’s Mosque while Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was at As-Sunh:

…فَقَامَ عُمَرُ يَقُولُ وَاللَّهِ مَا مَاتَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ‏.‏ قَالَتْ وَقَالَ عُمَرُ وَاللَّهِ مَا كَانَ يَقَعُ فِي نَفْسِي إِلَّا ذَاكَ وَلَيَبْعَثَنَّهُ اللَّهُ فَلَيَقْطَعَنَّ أَيْدِيَ رِجَالٍ وَأَرْجُلَهُمْ‏… فَقَالَ أَلَا مَنْ كَانَ يَعْبُدُ مُحَمَّدًا صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَإِنَّ مُحَمَّدًا قَدْ مَاتَ، وَمَنْ كَانَ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ… وَقَالَ {وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ}… فَنَشَجَ النَّاسُ يَبْكُونَ…

“…Hazrat Umar stood up declaring: ‘By Allah! The Messenger of Allah has not died!’ Umar later said: ‘By Allah, nothing else entered my heart except that.’ He proclaimed: ‘Allah will surely raise him up, and he will cut off the hands and feet of some men!’

Then Hazrat Abu Bakr arrived. He uncovered the face of the Messenger of Allah, kissed him, and said: ‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! You are pure in life and in death. By Allah, Allah will never make you taste two deaths.’

Hazrat Abu Bakr went out and addressed Hazrat Umar: ‘Calm down, O oath-taker!’ When Hazrat Abu Bakr spoke, Hazrat Umar sat down.

Hazrat Abu Bakr praised Allah and declared: ‘Whoever among you worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad has died. But whoever worshipped Allah, then Allah is Alive and never dies.’

Then he recited: ‘And Muhammad is only a Messenger. Verily, all Messengers have passed away before him…’ [Quran 3:144]. At this, the people wept bitterly…”

[Sahih al-Bukhari 3667, 3668]

3. Hazrat Umar’s (RA) Reasoning: The Analogy to Moses (AS)

Why did Hazrat Umar (RA) deny the Prophet’s ﷺ death? He believed the Prophet ﷺ had temporarily departed to his Lord, just like Moses (AS):

“When the Messenger of Allah passed away, Umar stood addressing the people and said: ‘Let me not hear anyone say that Muhammad has died. Verily, Muhammad has not died. Only his Lord has sent for him just as He sent for Moses, who was absent from his people for forty nights.‘”

[Ibn Sa’d, Kitab al-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. II, pp. 336–337] | Chain: Strong

Hazrat Umar (RA) did not claim the Prophet ﷺ was divine. He believed the Prophet ﷺ had gone temporarily to heaven and would return to punish the hypocrites.

4. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) Confirms the Decree of Death

Entering the chamber of his daughter Hazrat Aisha (RA), Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) verified the reality for himself:

…فَتَيَمَّمَ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَهُوَ مُسَجًّى بِبُرْدِ حِبَرَةٍ، فَكَشَفَ عَنْ وَجْهِهِ، ثُمَّ أَكَبَّ عَلَيْهِ فَقَبَّلَهُ ثُمَّ بَكَى فَقَالَ: بِأَبِي أَنْتَ يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، لَا يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ مَوْتَتَيْنِ، أَمَّا الْمَوْتَةُ الَّتِي كُتِبَتْ عَلَيْكَ فَقَدْ مُتَّهَا…

“…Hazrat Abu Bakr went straight to the Prophet, who was covered with a striped Yemenite cloth. He uncovered his face, bent over him, kissed him, and wept. He said: ‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Prophet of Allah! Allah will never combine two deaths upon you. As for the death decreed for you, you have now tasted it.’…”

[Sahih al-Bukhari 1241, 1242]

5. The First Appeal: General Verses Fail to Convince Hazrat Umar (RA)

Before ascending the pulpit, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) tried to reason with Hazrat Umar (RA) privately using general verses on human mortality:

…فَقَالَ: أَيُّهَا الرَّجُلُ، ارْبَعْ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ، فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَدْ مَاتَ، أَلَمْ تَسْمَعِ اللَّهَ يَقُولُ: { إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَيِّتُونَ } وَقَالَ: { وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ }…

“…Hazrat Abu Bakr said to him: ‘O man! Restrain yourself, for the Messenger of Allah has indeed died. Have you not heard Allah say: {Verily, you will die, and they will die} [Quran 39:30], and {We granted not to any human before you eternal life; if then you die, will they live forever?} [Quran 21:34]?’

Then Hazrat Abu Bakr ascended the pulpit, praised Allah, and recited: {Muhammad is only a Messenger. Verily, all Messengers have passed away before him…} [Quran 3:144]. Hazrat Abdullah bin Umar (RA) remarked: ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul! It was as though a veil had been lifted from our faces.'”

[Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah 37021]

Notice this critical historical fact: quoting general verses like Quran 39:30 (“You will die”) did not convince Hazrat Umar (RA). Hazrat Umar (RA) already believed the Prophet ﷺ would die eventually. He simply thought the Prophet ﷺ had gone temporarily to heaven like Moses (AS).

General statements about human mortality could not break his conviction. Only a verse proving that all past messengers had already passed away could settle the matter.

6. The Decisive Recitation of Quran 3:144 and the Acceptance of the Sahaba

When Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) recited Quran 3:144 from the pulpit, the impact was immediate and total:

…فَأَخْبَرَنِي سَعِيدُ بْنُ الْمُسَيَّبِ أَنَّ عُمَرَ قَالَ: وَاللَّهِ مَا هُوَ إِلَّا أَنْ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ تَلَاهَا فَعَقِرْتُ حَتَّى مَا تُقِلُّنِي رِجْلَايَ، وَحَتَّى أَهْوَيْتُ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ حِينَ سَمِعْتُهُ تَلَاهَا أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدْ مَاتَ‏.

“…Ibn Abbas reported: By Allah, it was as if the people had never known that Allah revealed this verse until Abu Bakr recited it. Every single person received it from him, and soon everyone was reciting it.

Sa’id bin al-Musayyib reported that Hazrat Umar said: ‘By Allah, the moment I heard Abu Bakr recite it, my legs gave way beneath me and I collapsed to the ground, realizing that the Prophet has indeed died.’“

[Sahih al-Bukhari 4452, 4453, 4454]

The Passing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: A Chronological Reconstruction

The historical sequence unfolds clearly across the authentic sources:

• The Final Illness: In his final moments, the Prophet ﷺ rested his head upon the shoulder of Hazrat Aisha (RA). A cold drop fell from his lips, and his breathing stopped. Believing he had fainted, she gently covered him with a sheet [Musnad Ahmad 25841].

• The Grief of Hazrat Umar (RA): Hazrat Umar (RA) and Mughirah bin Shu’bah (RA) entered the chamber. Seeing the Prophet ﷺ still, Hazrat Umar (RA) assumed he had merely lost consciousness [Musnad Ahmad 25841].

• The Initial Denial: At the door, Mughirah bin Shu’bah (RA) stated that the Prophet ﷺ had passed away. Distraught with grief, Hazrat Umar (RA) rejected this and declared the Prophet ﷺ would not die until Allah destroyed the hypocrites [Musnad Ahmad 25841].

• The Public Declaration: In the Mosque, Hazrat Umar (RA) drew his sword before the grieving crowd. He swore by Allah that the Prophet ﷺ was not dead [Sahih al-Bukhari 3667].

• The Moses (AS) Analogy: Hazrat Umar (RA) argued that the Prophet ﷺ had only departed temporarily, just as Moses (AS) disappeared for forty nights before returning to his people [Ibn Sa’d, Tabaqat, Vol. II, pp. 336–337].

• The Arrival of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA): Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) rode in swiftly from his dwelling in As-Sunh. He entered the chamber of Hazrat Aisha (RA) without speaking to the crowd [Sahih al-Bukhari 1241].

• The Certainty of Death: Uncovering the Prophet’s ﷺ face, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) kissed his forehead and wept. He stated: “Allah will never combine two deaths upon you. The death decreed for you has now been tasted” [Sahih al-Bukhari 1241].

• The Failed First Appeal: Coming outside, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) found Hazrat Umar (RA) still preaching his denial. He quietly reminded him of general verses on human mortality (Quran 39:30 and 21:34). Hazrat Umar (RA) remained unconvinced [Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah 37021].

• The Assembly Silenced: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) stepped up to the pulpit. He repeatedly urged Hazrat Umar (RA) to sit down, but he refused. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) then began praising Allah, and the entire gathering turned to him [Sahih al-Bukhari 1241].

• The Historic Proclamation: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) declared: “Whoever worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad has died. But whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is Alive and never dies” [Sahih al-Bukhari 1241].

• The Decisive Proof: He recited the universal divine law: “Muhammad is only a Messenger. Verily, all Messengers have passed away before him…” [Quran 3:144; Sahih al-Bukhari 1241].

• The Awakening of the Sahaba: It was as though the Companions had never heard this verse before. Immediately, every Companion took up the verse and recited it across the streets of Madinah [Sahih al-Bukhari 4452].

• The Submission of Hazrat Umar (RA): The theological reality struck Hazrat Umar (RA). His legs gave out beneath him and he collapsed to the earth, finally accepting that the Prophet ﷺ had died [Sahih al-Bukhari 4452].

• The Public Recantation: The next day from the pulpit, Hazrat Umar (RA) openly recanted his error. He admitted he had spoken out of intense personal longing, acknowledging that Allah’s decree had come to pass [Ibn Sa’d, Tabaqat, Vol. II, p. 338].

The Death of Isa (AS): The 8-Point Argument from Quran 3:144

The historical and linguistic facts of Quran 3:144 provide an airtight theological proof for the death of Isa (AS):

• The Universal Law of Messengers: Quran 3:144 explicitly establishes that messengers prior to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ have passed away (qad khalat). Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) cited this verse as absolute proof of the Prophet’s ﷺ death. If any past messenger were still alive, the proof would have collapsed immediately.

• The Two Exclusive Outcomes Defined by Allah: Within the verse itself, Allah defines khalat by two exhaustive states: dying naturally (māta) or being slain (qutila). Allah offers zero third option. There is no mention of bodily ascension into the clouds while remaining alive. If staying alive in heaven were a possibility for a prophet, Allah would have mentioned it here.

• The Grammatical Force of Al-Rusul (الرُّسُلُ): The noun Al-Rusul carries Lām al-Istighrāq (the definite article of total inclusiveness). It means every single messenger without exception. It does not mean “some messengers.” If it meant only “some,” it could never prove the Prophet’s ﷺ death, because he could simply have been one of the exceptions.

• Hazrat Umar’s (RA) Premise Was an Exception: Hazrat Umar (RA) was arguing an exceptional case. He claimed the Prophet ﷺ had departed temporarily like Moses (AS) on Mount Sinai. To refute an appeal to an exception, one must establish an absolute rule with zero exceptions. Quran 3:144 did exactly that.

• No Second Return to Earth: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) closed off the idea of a physical return before addressing the public. Kissing the Prophet’s ﷺ forehead, he stated: “Allah will never combine two deaths upon you.” A prophet does not leave, return decades or centuries later, and die a second time.

• The Unanimous Silence of the Sahaba (The First Ijma): When Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) recited Quran 3:144, hundreds of Companions were present. Not a single Companion stood up to say: “Wait Abu Bakr, not all messengers have died! Isa (AS) is alive in heaven and will return!” Their complete unanimous agreement (Ijmāʿ) proves they knew all past prophets had died.

• General Verses Were Not Enough: Verses like Quran 39:30 (“Verily you will die”) and Quran 21:34 (“We granted not to any human before you eternal life”) did not convince Hazrat Umar (RA). Why? Because those verses state that a prophet will eventually die, but do not rule out a temporary physical absence. Only Quran 3:144 convinced him, because it proved historical precedent: every single prophet before him had already passed away.

• The Burden of Proof is Absolute: Opponents claim that Isa (AS) did not die, but flew physically into the sky. There is zero Quranic verse and zero authentic Hadith stating Isa (AS) was exempted from Quran 3:144. To claim an exception without textual proof is baseless speculation.

Conclusion

The evidence from Quran 3:144 establishes an unshakeable Quranic reality:

• Quran 3:144 establishes an absolute rule: All messengers before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away.

• The verse defines its own terms: Khalat means natural death (māta) or martyrdom (qutila), leaving zero room for bodily ascension.

• Al-Rusul includes every prophet: Linguistically, Lām al-Istighrāq leaves zero exceptions among previous messengers.

• The first consensus of Islam: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) used this verse to prove the Prophet’s ﷺ death, and every Companion unanimously accepted it.

• Isa (AS) was a past messenger: As stated in Quran 5:75, Isa (AS) was a messenger before whom all messengers passed away.

• Isa (AS) has died: Since all messengers before Prophet Muhammad ﷺ died, Isa (AS) passed away like every other prophet.

There is zero verse in the Holy Quran and zero authentic Hadith stating that Isa (AS) was exempted from this divine law. The belief that Isa (AS) is physically alive in heaven contradicts the plain text of the Quran and the first unanimous consensus of the Companions.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does Quran 3:144 say about past prophets?

Quran 3:144 states: “Muhammad is only a Messenger. Verily, all Messengers have passed away [قَدْ خَلَتْ] before him.” The verse establishes that every prophet prior to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away through natural death (māta) or martyrdom (qutila).

What does Al-Rusul (الرُّسُلُ) mean in Quran 3:144?

The prefix Al- on Al-Rusul is Lām al-Istighrāq (the definite article of total inclusiveness). It signifies all messengers collectively and individually, leaving zero exceptions. If even one past prophet were still physically alive, the statement “all messengers have passed away before him” would be linguistically invalid.

How did Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) use Quran 3:144 after the Prophet’s ﷺ death?

When Hazrat Umar (RA) believed the Prophet ﷺ would return like Moses (AS), Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) addressed the Companions and recited Quran 3:144. Upon hearing it, all Companions—including Hazrat Umar (RA)—recognized that since all past messengers had died, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had also passed away. Zero Companions objected that Isa (AS) was still alive.

Introduction

In the early 1900s, an American preacher named Dr. John Alexander Dowie claimed to be the prophet Elijah (“Elijah the Restorer”). He built his own city, Zion City near Chicago, with thousands of followers and millions of dollars. From his pulpit, Dowie prayed daily for the total destruction of Islam.

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) challenged Dowie to a public prayer duel (Mubahala): let both men pray to God that whoever is the liar dies in the lifetime of the truthful one.

Dowie accepted the duel on September 26, 1903, when he publicly addressed the challenge in his magazine, called Ahmad (AS) a “fly”, and boasted that he would crush him under his foot.

God answered the duel:
1. Dowie was 11 years younger than Ahmad (AS), a multi-millionaire, and a faith healer claiming complete immunity from disease.
2. Ahmad (AS) was older, chronically ill, and lived in a remote Indian village.
3. Within four years of entering the duel, Dowie suffered two paralytic strokes, lost Zion City, went bankrupt, was disowned by his family, and died in misery on March 9, 1907—while Ahmad (AS) lived on in victory.

1901 – Dowie Claims to be Elijah and Attacks Islam

John Alexander Dowie founded the theocratic city of Zion, Illinois, in 1901. He claimed to be the “Messenger of the Covenant” and the third coming of Elijah.

On June 2, 1901, Dowie declared himself “Elijah the Restorer” before thousands in Chicago. He claimed that God gave him the power to heal all diseases and that doctors were tools of the devil.

On September 6, 1902, Munsey’s Magazine wrote about Dowie’s massive fame:

“Alexander Dowie ranks with the outstanding personalities who founded a new city capable of housing a million people. A city, which its founder proposes to convert into a spiritual headquarters of the whole world.”

[Munsey’s Magazine, September 6, 1902]

In his official weekly journal, Leaves of Healing, Dowie openly prayed for the destruction of all Muslims:

“Zion will have to wipe out that shocking blot upon humanity… May God help me to knock at the gate of the Moslem before long!”

[Leaves of Healing, Vol. 13, p. 474]

He wrote further:

“It is time that the Moslem abomination was gone, bag and baggage as Mr. Gladstone used to say. Let it slink away back into the deserts of Arabia whence the filthy thing emerged… May God destroy it.”

[Leaves of Healing, Vol. 12, p. 526]

For full details on Dowie’s early life and claims, read Who was John Alexander Dowie?.

September 1902 – Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) Challenges Dowie

When news of Dowie’s attacks reached Qadian, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) stepped forward to defend Islam.

In September 1902, Ahmad (AS) published his challenge in The Review of Religions (see the complete 1902 Challenge Text & Archival Scans):

“Whether the God of Muhammadans or the God of Dowie is the true God may be settled without the loss of millions of lives which Dr. Dowie’s prediction would involve… That method is that without threatening the Muhammadan public in general with destruction, he should choose me as his opponent and pray to God that of us two whoever is the liar may perish first.”

[The Review of Religions, Vol. 1, No. 9, September 1902, pp. 344–345]

Ahmad (AS) pointed out the facts:
* Dowie was 11 years younger than Ahmad (AS).
* Dowie claimed divine vitality and wealth; Ahmad (AS) was elderly and suffered from chronic illnesses.
* Death must not come through human violence, but directly through divine decree, such as disease, paralysis, or natural calamity.

June–August 1903 – American Press Reports the Challenge

In the summer of 1903, over 150 American and European newspapers published Ahmad (AS)’s challenge across the world.

The New York Commercial Advertiser reported in August 1903:

“Far, far away in India, comes a printed circular from Mirza Ghulam Ahmad who writes from Qadian in the Punjab. He has issued a challenge to Elijah III (Dowie)… In support of his claim, the Indian Messiah declares that when the Lord saw how badly things were being managed on earth, He raised him in the land of Punjab.”

[The New York Commercial Advertiser, August 1903]

You can see all 156 Historical Newspaper Scans & Clippings in our complete archive.

On August 23, 1903, Ahmad (AS) issued a follow-up warning in The Review of Religions:

“If the pretender to Elijahship shows his willingness by any direct or indirect means to enter the lists against me, he shall leave the world before my eyes with great sorrow and torment… Though he may try as hard as he can to fly from the death which awaits him, yet his flight from such a contest will be nothing less than death to him, and calamity will certainly overtake his Zion.”

[The Review of Religions, Vol. 2, No. 9, September 1903, p. 349]

September 26, 1903 – Dowie Enters the Duel and Calls Ahmad (AS) a “Fly”

On September 26, 1903, Dowie publicly responded to the challenge in Leaves of Healing. He admitted receiving the letters from Qadian and accepted the duel through his boast:

“In India, there is a foolish Messiah who writes to me often telling me that the tomb of Jesus Christ is in Kashmir, and people sometimes say to me, why do you not reply to this, that or the other thing? Reply! Do you think that I shall reply to these gnats and flies. If I put my foot on them, I would crush out their lives. I give them a chance to fly away and live.”

[Leaves of Healing, September 26, 1903]

By declaring to his followers that he would crush Ahmad (AS) under his foot, Dowie officially entered the prayer duel.

October 1903 – Dowie’s Collapse at Madison Square Garden

Just three weeks after boasting that he would crush Ahmad (AS), Dowie took 4,000 followers to New York City for a massive crusade at Madison Square Garden.

The crusade ended in total disaster:
* Dowie lost control of his voice and stammered on stage.
* The audience jeered, and thousands walked out during his speeches.
* The New York Times reported on October 19, 1903: “THRONGS TURN FROM ENRAGED ‘ELIJAH III.’… Pleadings and Even Force Have No Effect on Thousands Who Decline to Wait for Dowie’s Preaching” [Scan].
* The New York Times reported on October 20, 1903: “HOSTILE AUDIENCE HOWLS AT DOWIE… During the scene of pandemonium the voice of Dowie died away, and he completely lost control of the audience” [Scan].
* The New York Times reported on October 24, 1903: “DOWIE LEAVES CITY AND MAY NOT RETURN… Restoration Host Disintegrating” [Part 1] [Part 2].

The failed crusade plunged Zion City into over $300,000 of debt.

1904 – Dowie’s Failed World Tour

In 1904, Dowie traveled to Australia, Germany, and England to regain his reputation. The tour was another failure:
* In Australia, hotels refused to host him.
* In Germany, the American Embassy refused to introduce him to Kaiser Wilhelm.
* In England, public protests forced him to leave under police protection.

September–December 1905 – Dowie Struck by Paralysis

In September 1905, while preaching on stage in Zion, Dowie suddenly collapsed from a severe paralytic stroke.

In December 1905, a second stroke left him permanently crippled.

The man who claimed he could heal any disease by prayer and called doctors tools of Satan was now completely bedridden and had to be carried on a stretcher.

April 1906 – Zion Revolts and Deposes Dowie

While Dowie was in Mexico attempting to recover, his chief deputy, Wilbur Glenn Voliva, led a revolt in Zion City in April 1906:
* Dowie was removed from leadership and excommunicated from his church.
* Church audits revealed Dowie had stolen over $2.5 million and kept secret stashes of alcohol.
* His wife, Jane Dowie, and his son, Gladstone Dowie, publicly deserted him.
* Dowie was evicted from his home (Shiloh House) and left penniless.

February 20, 1907 – The Revelation of the “Great Victory”

On February 20, 1907, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) published a fresh revelation from God in Qadian:

“God has informed me: I will reveal a fresh sign which will be a great victory. This will be a sign for the whole world.”

[Tadhkirah, Revelation of February 20, 1907]

March 9, 1907 – Dowie Dies in Disgrace while Ahmad (AS) Lives

Seventeen days later, on March 9, 1907, Dr. John Alexander Dowie died in Zion City at age 59.

He died paralyzed, penniless, deserted by his family, and mentally broken.

The news was telegraphed globally. Indian newspapers published the news immediately, including The Pioneer (Allahabad, March 11, 1907), The Civil and Military Gazette (Lahore, March 12, 1907), and The Indian Daily Telegraph (Lucknow, March 12, 1907).

Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS), living in good health at over 70 years of age, survived Dowie and witnessed the complete victory.

In May 1907, Hazrat Ahmad (AS) documented the fulfillment in his book Haqiqat-ul-Wahi:

ڈوئی کے بارے میں مَیں نے بار بار شائع کیا تھا کہ وہ میری زندگی میں ہی ہلاک ہو جائے گا اور وہ نہایت حسرت اور عذاب کے ساتھ مارا جائے گا چنانچہ ایسا ہی ہوا۔

“Regarding Dowie, I had repeatedly published that he would perish during my lifetime and would die in great sorrow and torment; and so it happened.”

[Haqiqat-ul-Wahi, Ruhani Khaza’in, Vol. 22, p. 506]

American Newspapers Acknowledge the Victory

American newspapers recognized the exact fulfillment of the duel.

The Princeton Telegraph summarized Dowie’s fall on March 20, 1907 [Scan]:

“When John Alexander Dowie passed away, death ended the most spectacular and remarkable career that modern times have known. Gigantic successes and tragic failures punctuated his life. Here are some of the remarkable works and reversals that marked Dowie’s career:

• He built a creed: he was excommunicated.

• He built a city: he was exiled from it.

• He amassed a fortune of millions: he was reduced to virtual poverty.

• He elevated Voliva to great power: Voliva ruined him.

• He drew about him thousands who worshiped him: he died deserted by all save a handful of the faithful.”

[Princeton Telegraph, March 20, 1907]

The Sunday Herald (Boston) published on June 23, 1907 [Part 1] [Part 2] [Part 3]:

“Great Is Mirza Ghulam Ahmad The Messiah FORETOLD PATHETIC END OF DOWIE… He called the turn on Dowie, and why may he not on devastation?”

[The Sunday Herald, Boston, June 23, 1907]

In April 1907, The Review of Religions published its victory statement (see Ahmad’s (AS) 1907 Proclamation of Victory & Scans):

“In bringing disaster upon Dowie’s head and ultimately in his untimely death brought about with sorrow and torment, Almighty God has given His judgment exactly as He had informed His Messenger three or four years previous to these occurrences. It is a judgment which distinguishes the true Messenger of God from a false claimant, the true one from an impostor.”

[The Review of Religions, Vol. 6, No. 4, April 1907, pp. 117–120]

The Living Sign: The Fath-e-Azeem Mosque in Zion (2022)

In October 2022, Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad (ABA), the Fifth Caliph of the Promised Messiah, traveled to Zion, Illinois.

His Holiness inaugurated the Fath-e-Azeem Mosque (“The Great Victory”) in Zion City. During the inauguration, the Mayor of Zion presented His Holiness with the key to the city. The city that Dowie founded to wipe out Islam is now home to an active Ahmadiyya mosque.

Read the 2022 Keynote Address by Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad (ABA) in Zion, Illinois.

Summary

• The prayer duel: Ahmad (AS) challenged Dowie to a prayer duel (Mubahala) after Dowie prayed for the destruction of all Muslims.

• Dowie entered the duel: On September 26, 1903, Dowie mocked Ahmad (AS) as a “fly” to be crushed, officially accepting the contest.

• Massive physical disparity: Dowie was 11 years younger and a faith healer; Ahmad (AS) was older and chronically ill.

• Complete ruin: Within four years, Dowie suffered two strokes, lost Zion City, went bankrupt, and died on March 9, 1907—while Ahmad (AS) survived him in good health.

• Verified by American newspapers: Over 150 newspapers reported the duel and confirmed Ahmad (AS)’s victory.

Conclusion

The prayer duel between Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (AS) and John Alexander Dowie is a clear historical sign of the truth of Islam.

When Dowie prayed to destroy Islam, God answered through the Promised Messiah (AS). Dowie lost his health, wealth, city, family, and life. Today, Dowie’s church has disappeared, while the Fath-e-Azeem Mosque stands in Zion City as living proof of God’s victory.

Introduction

Opponents of the Jamaat claim that the Promised Messiah (as) received several ‘blasphemous revelations’. The Promised Messiah (as) will sometimes give the interpretation of the revelations right underneath them yet they will refuse to show this as it exposes the fallaciousness of their arguments. As we will see, their entire argument is based off selective quotations and deception.

Revelations to the Prophet (saw)

The Prophet (saw) was described metaphorically as being one with Allah (swt):

فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ ۚ وَلِيُبْلِىَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ بَلَآءً حَسَنًا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ ١٧

It was not you ˹believers˺ who killed them, but it was Allah Who did so. Nor was it you ˹O Prophet˺ who threw ˹a handful of sand at the disbelievers˺, but it was Allah Who did so, rendering the believers a great favour. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Al-Anfal (8:17)

The Prophet’s (saw) hand being over the hands of the believers is described as Allah’s hand being over them:

إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ ۚ فَمَن نَّكَثَ فَإِنَّمَا يَنكُثُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِمَا عَـٰهَدَ عَلَيْهُ ٱللَّهَ فَسَيُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًۭا ١٠

Surely those who pledge allegiance to you ˹O Prophet˺ are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. Allah’s Hand is over theirs. Whoever breaks their pledge, it will only be to their own loss. And whoever fulfils their pledge to Allah, He will grant them a great reward.

Al-Fath (48:10)

He is commanded to call the believers ‘his servants’:

قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ فِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌۭ ۗ وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌ ۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّـٰبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍۢ ١٠

Say ˹O Prophet˺, “O My servants who believe! Be mindful of your Lord. Those who do good in this world will have a good reward. And Allah’s earth is spacious. Only those who endure patiently will be given their reward without limit.”

Az-Zumar (39:10)

Names of Allah are only in the Quran or Hadith?

The argument that the only names of God that exist are those within the Quran and Sunnah is completely incorrect. The Prophet (saw) explicitly accepted the existence of names taught to creation and that Allah had kept to himself.

اللّهُـمَّ إِنِّي عَبْـدُكَ ابْنُ عَبْـدِكَ ابْنُ أَمَتِـكَ نَاصِيَتِي بِيَـدِكَ مَاضٍ فِيَّ حُكْمُكَ عَدْلٌ فِيَّ قَضَاؤكَ أَسْأَلُـكَ بِكُلِّ اسْمٍ هُوَ لَكَ سَمَّـيْتَ بِهِ نَفْسَكَ أِوْ أَنْزَلْتَـهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ أَوْ عَلَّمْـتَهُ أَحَداً مِنْ خَلْقِـكَ أَوِ اسْتَـأْثَرْتَ بِهِ فِي عِلْمِ الغَيْـبِ عِنْـدَكَ أَنْ تَجْـعَلَ القُرْآنَ رَبِيـعَ قَلْبِـي وَنورَ صَـدْرِي وجَلَاءَ حُـزْنِي وذَهَابَ هَمِّـي
O Allah, I am Your slave, and the son of Your male slave, and the son of your female slave. My forehead is in Your Hand (i.e. you have control over me). Your Judgment upon me is assured, and Your Decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every Name that You have named Yourself with, revealed in Your Book, taught any one of Your creation, or kept unto Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen that is with You, to make the Qur’an the spring of my heart, and the light of my chest, the banisher of my sadness, and the reliever of my distress.
Reference: Ahmad 1/391, and Al-Albani graded it authentic.

Hisn al-Muslim 120

Core Revelation

This is the core revelation from where several allegations trace themselves to. We will address other allegations not found in this as well:

You are from Me and I am from you. The heaven and earth are with you as they are with Me. You are from Our water and the others are from dryness and you are to Me as My Uniqueness and you are to Me in a state of communion that is not known to anyone in the creation. God praises you from His throne. You have proceeded from Him and He has chosen you out of the whole world. You have a high station in My presence. I have chosen you for Myself. You are the light of the world. Wonderful is your status. I shall raise you to Myself, and shall grant dominance to your Community up to the Day of Judgment. You have been blessed and God has raised your status. You are God’s dignity, so He will not forsake you. You are the eternal word, so you will not be wiped out. I shall come to you with My hosts. My property, which had been plundered, will be bestowed on you. I shall honour you and guard you.

[Kitabul-Bariyyah, part 1, pp.75-77, First Edition, Rühäni Khaza’in, vol. 13, pp. 100-103]

‘You are from Me and I am from you’

This language is frequently used to describe attachment/detachment to a people and does not refer to physical fatherhood/sonship. The Quran states that those who follow someone is from them.

رَبِّ إِنَّهُنَّ أَضْلَلْنَ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ ۖ فَمَن تَبِعَنِى فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّى ۖ وَمَنْ عَصَانِى فَإِنَّكَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ ٣٦

My Lord! They have caused many people to go astray. So whoever follows me is from me, and whoever disobeys me—then surely You are ˹still˺ All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Ibrahim (14:36)

A Hadith in Bukhari states that the Ash’ari tribe are from the Prophet (saw) and he is from them, however they were not of the same tribe. This is because the Prophet (saw) was referring to obedience/attachment.

حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ أُسَامَةَ، عَنْ بُرَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي بُرْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي مُوسَى، قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏”‏ إِنَّ الأَشْعَرِيِّينَ إِذَا أَرْمَلُوا فِي الْغَزْوِ، أَوْ قَلَّ طَعَامُ عِيَالِهِمْ بِالْمَدِينَةِ جَمَعُوا مَا كَانَ عِنْدَهُمْ فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاحِدٍ، ثُمَّ اقْتَسَمُوهُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي إِنَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ بِالسَّوِيَّةِ، فَهُمْ مِنِّي وَأَنَا مِنْهُمْ ‏”‏‏.‏

Narrated Abu Musa: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, “When the people of Ash`ari tribe ran short of food during the holy battles, or the food of their families in Medina ran short, they would collect all their remaining food in one sheet and then distribute it among themselves equally by measuring it with a bowl. So, these people are from me, and I am from them.”

Sahih al-Bukhari 2486

‘You are from Our water and they are from dryness’

The opponents deceptively do not show that the Promised Messiah (as) himself explained the meaning of this revelation to refer to the water of faith not the semen of God (God forbid!)

In the revelation: ‘You are from Our water and they are from (fashal)’; by water is meant the water of faith, steadfastness, righteousness, loyalty, sincerity, and the love of God which is bestowed only by God. (fashal) means cowardice, which proceeds from Satan and is at the root of all faithlessness and viciousness. When steadfastness is lost a person leans towards sin. Thus cowardice proceeds from Satan and the water of righteous doctrine and pure conduct proceeds from God Almighty. When a child is conceived, if it is fortunate and destined to be righteous it is taken under the protection of Ruhul-Qudus [spirit of holiness] and if it is unfortunate and is destined to be vicious it is under the shadow of Satan. Satan has a part in it, and metaphorically it is called the progeny of Satan. And those who belong to God are attributed to Him; they have, in earlier scriptures, been metaphorically called sons of God.

[Anjam-e-Atham, pp. 56–57 footnote, Ruhani Khaza’in, vol. 11, pp. 56–57 footnote]

The same phrase ‘water of the heavens’ has been used to refer to the companions of the Prophet (saw):

حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ تَلِيدٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ‏{‏قَالَ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏}‏ ‏”‏ لَمْ يَكْذِبْ إِبْرَاهِيمُ إِلاَّ ثَلاَثَ كَذَبَاتٍ بَيْنَمَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ مَرَّ بِجَبَّارٍ وَمَعَهُ سَارَةُ ـ فَذَكَرَ الْحَدِيثَ ـ فَأَعْطَاهَا هَاجَرَ قَالَتْ كَفَّ اللَّهُ يَدَ الْكَافِرِ وَأَخْدَمَنِي آجَرَ ‏”‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ فَتِلْكَ أُمُّكُمْ يَا بَنِي مَاءِ السَّمَاءِ‏.‏

Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Abraham did not tell lies except three. (One of them was) when Abraham passed by a tyrant and (his wife) Sara was accompanying him (Abu Huraira then mentioned the whole narration and said: ) (The tyrant) gave her Hajar. Sara said, “Allah saved me from the hands of the Kafir (i.e. infidel) and gave me Hajar to serve me.” (Abu Huraira added: ) That (Hajar) is your mother, O Banu Ma’-As-Sama’ (i.e., the Arabs).

Sahih al-Bukhari 5084

“قال كثيرون المراد ببني ماء السماء العرب كلهم لخلوص نسبهم وصفائه…”

“Many have said: The intended meaning of ‘sons of the water of the sky’ is all of the Arabs, due to the purity and clarity of their lineage…“

[Sahih Muslim bi Sharh al-Nawawi, Vol. 15, p. 125, 1st Edition, 1349 AH / 1930 CE]

‘You are to me like my unity’

The opponents one again refuse to mention the interpretation given to this by the Promised Messiah (as) as meaning that he is close to Allah (swt) and that Allah (swt) loves him.

“انت منی بمنزلة توحیدی وتفریدی فحان ان تعان وتعرف بین الناس۔ یعنی تو مجھ سے ایسا قرب رکھتا ہے اور ایسا ہی میں تجھے چاہتا ہوں جیسا کہ اپنی توحید اور تفرید کو سو جیسا کہ میں اپنی توحید کی شہرت چاہتا ہوں ایسا ہی تجھے دنیا میں مشہور کروں گا۔ اور ہر ایک جگہ جو میرا نام جائے گا تیرا نام بھی ساتھ ہوگا۔”

“You are to Me like My Unity and My Singularity, so the time has come for you to be helped and made known among the people. Meaning, you hold such closeness to Me, and I love you just as [I love] My Unity and Singularity. So, just as I desire the renown of My Unity, similarly I will make you famous in the world. And everywhere My name goes, your name will also accompany it.”

[Ruhani Khazain, Vol. 17, Zamima Tuhfa Golarviyya, p. 61]

‘You have proceeded from him’

This does not entail fatherhood at all. The Quran refers to Jesus as a word that proceeded from Allah (swt).

يَـٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ لَا تَغْلُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُۥٓ أَلْقَىٰهَآ إِلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌۭ مِّنْهُ ۖ فَـَٔامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦ ۖ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ ثَلَـٰثَةٌ ۚ ٱنتَهُوا۟ خَيْرًۭا لَّكُمْ ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَـٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ سُبْحَـٰنَهُۥٓ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌۭ ۘ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًۭا ١٧١

O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes regarding your faith; say nothing about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of Allah and the fulfilment of His Word through Mary and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, “Trinity.” Stop!—for your own good. Allah is only One God. Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son! To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs.
